newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dollar, drugs to boost Akzo Nobel Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: Dollar, drugs to boost Akzo Nobel Q1 net.

text.p: First-quarter net earnings at Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel NV will get a healthy lift from strong profit growth in high-margin coatings and pharmaceuticals as well as a stronger dollar, analysts said on Monday.

Due to report on Friday, Akzo is seen posting first-quarter ordinary net of between 332-380 million guilders, with consensus at 363 million. In the year-earlier quarter, net earnings from ordinary operations amounted to 332 million.
"Operating profits at the pharmaceuticals division are set to mushroom some 26 percent to 229 million guilders," said Nils van Elzelingen, chemicals analyst with NIB Securities.

A stronger dollar would account for some seven percent of the rise, while profit growth would also be helped by lower start-up costs for new products, an upturn in oral contraceptive sales and structural growth of some seven to eight percent.

Coatings were also seen booking sharply higher operating profits in the first quarter, although the rate of profit growth was set to slow in the traditionally high-turnover second and third quarters, Van Elzelingen said.
Peter Beijers of Kempen and Co also identified pharmaceuticals and coatings as the main growth areas.
"I see coatings performing better year-on-year, mainly because the synergy advantages of the Akzo-Nobel merger were not yet apparent in the first quarter of 1996," he said.
Raw material prices were also lower than in the year-earlier quarter, he added.
Beijers said the stronger dollar would also help Akzo's chemicals division, while the operating result at fibres would likely come in slightly lower year-on-year.
Patrick Rutten of F. Van Lanschot Bankiers agreed, but said that restructuring at the poorly performing unit was starting to pay off.

"But coatings will be the big money-spinner, due in part to the milder winter this year and a rise in sales prices," he predicted. "I expect operating profits at the division to rise to some 135 million guilders from 81 million last year."
Analysts said renewed reports of contraceptive pill-related health risks which surfaced in the media last week were not expected to have a major impact on future Akzo profits.
"I think it will have a limited effect, although obviously this renewed controversy is not pleasant," NIB's Van Elzelingen said.
He added that, in the long term, Akzo was bound to be proved right in its assertion that the risks of thrombosis associated with the low-dosage mini-pill were negligible.

"I see no reason to adjust my second-quarter estimates," agreed Kempen's Beijers. "Last year, too, we saw that other products were able to sufficiently compensate for the fall in pill sales." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
